questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you see a police officer.
When another vehicle is following you too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another vehicle is following you too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down if another vehicle is following you too closely. This warns the other driver that you are slowing down. It is also helpful to flash your brake light when you need to slow down where other drivers might not expect it.

questions.question: What should you do on a long trip?

options.text: Try to take as few breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel drowsy.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold, wind, and rain.
Ride more than 12 hours in one day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold, wind, and rain.
questions.explanation: Protect yourself from the elements like cold, wind, and rain to reduce fatigue. Limit your riding to no more than six hours per day and take breaks every two hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants because they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: How should you navigate a curve on a three-wheeled motorcycle?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve itself. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: What should riders do when traveling in a group?

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together while keeping enough space around each rider. This makes the group easier to see and prevents riders from becoming separated. Riding in pairs does not allow enough room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: Where you are most likely to be seen and can keep a safe space around you.
Where you can draft off other vehicles.
Where you can change positions most often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you are most likely to be seen and can keep a safe space around you.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the lane where other drivers can see you and you have enough space around you for safety.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distance. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. It takes longer to realize the vehicle has stopped, and you need extra time to stop safely.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols.
Blue with white lettering or symbols.
White with black lettering or symbols.
White with red lettering or symbols.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see and be seen, avoid blind spots and hazards, and discourage other drivers from sharing your lane. Most importantly, it should give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle rider adjust for being harder to see at night?

options.text: Reduce your speed when riding at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle so its headlights light you up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when riding at night.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, increase your following distance, and use the headlights of other vehicles to help you see ahead. Use your high beam headlight unless you are following or meeting another vehicle, and be flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: The child does not need to reach the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the rider.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit directly behind the rider. A child in front may not balance properly and could interfere with the rider's control of the motorcycle.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of the following do you NOT need to adjust?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This changes how the bike sits. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. You do not need to adjust brake light position.

questions.question: How long can the effects of marijuana last?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana affects you within minutes and effects last two to four hours. Eaten marijuana takes over an hour to start working but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: Hand signals show turns or stops. When your left arm is bent at the elbow and points downward, it means you plan to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps others see you best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding so others can see you. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green are best. Dark colors are harder to see.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake
Brake and swerve at the same time
Choose to either brake or swerve
Do not swerve and only use the front brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake
questions.explanation: Do the actions one at a time. Do not brake while swerving. Braking and swerving together can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
Pull onto the shoulder of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: The center of the lane has oil deposits that are slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: If a driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them
Pull over to the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down. The tailgater is focused on you and may not see hazards ahead that require traffic to slow down.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust which of the following?
questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You must adjust the shocks to handle this extra weight. The motorcycle will sit at a different angle, so also adjust the headlight and mirrors.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work well, it must:

options.text: Block all air from passing through
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield has no scratches, resists damage, allows clear views to both sides, fastens securely, lets air through to prevent fogging, and has room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots
Invite other drivers to share your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and provides an escape route if needed.
